title: Tiimely Home Loans
body:
O.P.
Thinking of refinancing from Bankwest over to Tictoc home loans, very competitive variable rate and virtually no application fees (other than the usual government fees) anyone used them. I see from their website they are supported by Bendigo bank.

---- replies ----
[User #46555161 postsdm1432Participant] O.P.
Well decided to take the plunge and apply for the 22minute home loan through their website (refinance) very easy to navigate, prompt decision had a delay due to a lower desktop valuation. Valuer came out (no cost to me), report submtted same day and contract for loan emailed two hours laterr (less than a week!).
Pity Bankwest couldn't offer me anything to remain with them (all I asked was not to pay the package fee $395!-nope they are happy to see a long serving customer leave with a 500k repayment/interest loan). May even decide to move my whole banking from them.
Looks if Tictoc use Adelaide/Bendigo bank for the finance, hopefully they will be okay?
Service from Tictoc spot on, prompt and refreshing if anyone is thinking about them , excellent rates best of all minimum fees.
[User #1125491813 postsaleayrWhirlpool Enthusiast] Be interested to see whether they do any of the other cheap non-bank tricks, such as raising your interest rate quicker than the advertised rate on the website to attract new customers.
I was with State Custodians and they moved my rate a few times out of step with the rate on their website. 1 rate to suck you in with, and then hope you don't leave when they increase it slowly.
[User #46555161 postsdm1432Participant] O.P.
BendiGus writes...
Are you paying the $10 per month fee for offset. Or have they waived th
Haven't crossed that bridge yet or thought about the off set account, once loan set up will ask the question with the bank.
[User #6152863926 postsJamie.M Brokerwww.passgo.com.auWhirlpool Forums Addict] aleayr writes...
I was with State Custodians and they moved my rate a few times out of step with the rate on their website. 1 rate to suck you in with, and then hope you don't leave when they increase it slowly.
Yep – I see it happen quite a bit with cheap online lenders :-(
The larger/second tier lenders are extremely competitive at the moment – personally, I aim for a large package discount with a major rather than the cheapest rate from an online lender.
Cheers
Jamie
[User #306736158 poststhminhducForum Regular] Anyone approved with a loan? Have they performed settlement for you? What has been your experience so far? Thank you.
[User #46555161 postsdm1432Participant] O.P.
thminhduc writes...
Anyone approved with a loan? Have they performed settlement for you? What has been your experience so far? Thank you.
G'day, currently going through settlement with their preferred solicitors Leadpoint in QLD all paperwork electronic printed off and posted back, they received today so see how long they take. Tictoc no issues with them, like their communication and speed in which they processed my online application. They use Bank of Adelaide for the actual mortgage funds, not sure what they are like as I am currently with Bankwest (who as I say didn't really do or offer me anything to retain our bussiness- which is disappointing really).
[User #263964910 postsBlinkyBillWhirlpool Forums Addict] Has anyone been with Tic Toc for some time? Is there advertised rate a honeymoon rate? Have they increased rates for existing borrowers while still advertising lower rates for new applicants. I've heard this has occurred with another non-bank lender "State Custodians".
If they did increase their rates over and above what was reasonable, would the only penalty of using them be the discharge fee if refinancing with another home loan provider who didn't charge application fees.
Any dodgy terms and conditions with Tic Toc?
[User #249161131 postsevalordForum Regular] thinking about going with them, can anyone provide feedback? A lot of small player jack up rates shortly after signing up.
[User #59947172 postsJakeParticipant] Submitted an application yesterday. It wasnt automatically approved and I had to wait for a call back. The guy told me on the phone that I needed at least 70% LVM (not 80% as advertised) because my property was in a high complex (anything over 5 stories or 50 properties). As I am at 75% I told him I couldnt make 70%. The guy 'withdrew' my application, and I got an email worded as if it was my choice. Not sure if that is a benefit to me or them – why not 'reject' the application? I little disappointed.
[User #8032331210 postsOzangelIn the penalty box] this post was edited
Detective Randal writes...
Not sure if that is a benefit to me or them – why not 'reject' the application? I little disappointed.
Better also keep an eye on your credit file. I applied with TicToc but didn't finalise my application. Someone called to follow up and I said I wanted to cancel. Later on I found out they did a credit check on me anyway. It's in my credit file.

[User #46555161 postsdm1432Participant] O.P.
michael j Why would they waive it?
They said the rate was competitive and wouldn't budge, not even a follow up call to "talk me in to staying" shame really as it was a loan over 500k paid on time and up to date. TicToc no issues with them delivered what they said they would in 4 weeks to completion, minimum outlay without any hiccups along the way. They are Just a middle man for Bendigo & Adelaide bank with a cheaper rate.
[User #6472041272 postsWoodchipsPhysio GeekWhirlpool Enthusiast] michael j writes...
You're not paying a package fee for fun. You are getting MORE than $395 of benefit for that amount. Why would they waive it?
I was with Bankwest before I refinanced away.
I was getting 3.92% on a 400k+ loan. I had to pay a $395 package fee to get it. I had a 100% offset account and a rewards credit card.
Cost of the card = $100 per annum. Cost of the offset account = $0 per annum Remaining package fee = $295 for worse than market interest rate.
---
I currently am with a provider that costs me $0 per annum 3.54% on 400k+ balance 100% offset with debit card access
And have a third party credit card that costs me effectively nothing $129 per annum Velocity Frequent flyer card with annual $129 flight gift card.
So no, most people can see that they're not getting any significant benefit from that package fee compared to the rest of the lending market.
